Rain puddle vast as an inland sea, canopy reflected in it with photographic precision, a single drowned ginkgo leaf resting on the bottom in perfect golden silhouette, the surface just trembling where a drop from a fern tip is still falling.

Cycad crown seen from directly beneath, every frond radiating outward like the ribs of a vaulted ceiling, backlit so the leaflets burn electric green along their edges, and at the very centre a new frond coiled tight as a fist, just beginning to open.

Moss in full living depth, the surface a landscape of hummocks and valleys, every hummock a different green from chartreuse to almost black, dew caught in the nap like thousands of tiny lanterns, a corridor of lower ground between two ridges running straight into the shade.

Horsetail stems at flood margin, packed so tightly the gaps between them form a maze of green corridors, each jointed stem throwing a short sharp shadow on the next, the water between the outermost stems perfectly still, holding a broken reflection of the green above.

Root buttress as a great climbing wall, its face seamed with cracks where liverwort has taken hold in long green stripes, the archway at its base worn smooth and dark, a snail track dried to a silver ribbon crossing the threshold and continuing into the dim passage beyond.

Moss landscape in deep green shade interrupted by one low beam of light striking a single hummock and igniting it from within, the dew-drops on that one hummock burning white while every surrounding surface stays cool and dim, depth of field falling away fast in every direction.

Deep ginkgo-leaf litter, the fans overlapping in gold and pale yellow, some still holding their lobed shape and others crumbling at the tips, one intact leaf tent-pitched on two rolled neighbours making a low cave, a groove of trapped rainwater running along its central fold still bright.

Mossy log-top ridge, the moss so saturated it is almost turquoise, individual moss-stems visible at this scale as tiny trees, a line of bracket fungi along the log's spine serving as a staircase, the space beneath the lowest bracket a dry amber-lit alcove in the damp green world.
